title: Challenge Details: Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions
description: Full challenge brief detailing the mission problem, background, objectives, and UI/feature considerations.

title: 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
description: Basic information from NASA's Human Research Program on the five primary environmental hazards that affect humans during space missions (Radiation, Isolation/Confinement, Distance, Gravity Fields, Hostile Environments).

title: Risks of Human Spaceflight
description: Comprehensive mapping of the human physiological, behavioral, and clinical risks tracked by NASA HRP, cross-referenced with countermeasures and flight elements.

title: Ongoing HRP Research in Space
description: Articles, findings, and ongoing experiments aboard the International Space Station, ground analogs (HERA, bed rest), and future Artemis exploration missions.

title: Monitoring Radiation for Astronaut Health
description: Highlights Canadian technologies and research (such as the Canadian Active Neutron Spectrometer - CANS) used to autonomously monitor radiation exposure on the ISS and future Moon/Mars missions.

title: Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?
description: Explains how microgravity accelerates physiological changes analogous to aging and sedentary lifestyle (bone loss, muscle atrophy, cardiovascular changes, diabetes risk) and how space experiments advance medicine on Earth.
